Templates: plan-*

Node types: plan-doc, plan-task, plan-step, plan-check — four templates, one file, nested three deep, per the family-file convention
File naming: this file is plan.template.html, named after the plan-* family it defines. Documents that conform to plan-doc are named <date>-<topic>.plan.html
Purpose: the shape an implementation plan takes when written as a v4 node instead of the superpowers:writing-plans skill's default Markdown — the same override spec.template.html already made for superpowers:brainstorming's spec output
Sibling of: knowledge.template.html, spec.template.html
Styling: ./plan.template.css, this family's own rendering rules, plus the shared ../theme.css every document links

Four nested conforming types, not one flat schema

plan-doc contains plan-tasks, each independently conforming to #plan-task; plan-task contains plan-steps, each conforming to #plan-step; plan-step contains at most one plan-check, conforming to #plan-check. This is the same pattern spec.template.html's own "Conformance" section documents: a document can have any number of typed elements nested inside it, each independently addressable via its own data-conforms-to. A parent's own <template> only ever declares a nested child tag as "may be present" — it can't reach into that child's own internal shape, which is why each of the three nested types needs its own data-conforms-to: pnpm validate's crawler finds every validatable instance purely by scanning for [data-conforms-to] anywhere in the tree.

plan-title/plan-status repeat across all three nesting levels (doc, task, step) — fields belong to the family, not to one type within it, same as every other family here. This is exactly the scenario that required fixing template.template.html's generic validator to scope its field lookups to direct children only, rather than searching an instance's entire subtree.

The four types

plan-doc

Fields: title, status, date, goal, architecture, optional tech-stack, optional global-constraints, optional (repeatable) plan-task children.

<plan-doc data-conforms-to="./plan.template.html#plan-doc">
  <plan-title>…</plan-title>
  <plan-status>active</plan-status>
  <plan-date>2026-07-25</plan-date>
  <plan-goal>…</plan-goal>
  <plan-architecture>…</plan-architecture>
</plan-doc>

plan-task

Fields: title, status, files, optional interfaces, optional (repeatable) plan-step children.

<plan-task id="task-1" data-conforms-to="./plan.template.html#plan-task">
  <plan-title>…</plan-title>
  <plan-status>pending</plan-status>
  <plan-files>Create: …</plan-files>
</plan-task>

plan-step

Fields: title, status (narrower enum than doc/task — a single step is only ever done or not), optional detail, optional plan-check child.

<plan-step id="task-1-step-1" data-conforms-to="./plan.template.html#plan-step">
  <plan-title>Write the failing test</plan-title>
  <plan-status>pending</plan-status>
</plan-step>

plan-check

Fields: command, optional success (enum true|false, code default "true" when absent), optional output (a plain substring match).

<plan-check data-conforms-to="./plan.template.html#plan-check">
  <plan-check-command>pytest tests/foo.py::test_bar -v</plan-check-command>
  <plan-check-success>false</plan-check-success>
  <plan-check-output>function not defined</plan-check-output>
</plan-check>

This section actually runs

One realistic nested instance (a doc containing a task containing a step containing a check), checked by a locally-defined direct-children-scoped validator — duplicated rather than imported, the same way knowledge.template.html's own live-demo validator duplicates rather than imports (a browser-loaded module has no reliable way to import across files over file://). The real authoritative check is pnpm validate, which does use the real shared validateFromTemplate under Node.

Sample plan active 2026-07-25 Build the thing. Do it in a few small steps. Sample task active Create: src/thing.ts Sample step pending echo ok true 
running...

Authoring commands

add and update each take a kind (doc, task, or step) as their own first positional argument and dispatch internally — the same convention knowledge add <type> already established, reused here instead of four separate hyphenated command names, which JavaScript can't export as plain identifiers.
